tip: Куда (kuda = where to) asks about direction with motion verbs, unlike где (gde = where) for a fixed location.
The -ся on открывается (otkryvaetsya = opens) makes it intransitive: the door opens by itself, no object needed.
вёз (vyoz) is past of везти (vezti = carry by vehicle), used when the load moves by transport, not carried by hand.
The -ся on целуются (tseluyutsya = kiss) is reciprocal: they kiss each other, not themselves.
A place entered with на (na) is exited with с (s), not из (iz): с вечеринки (s vecherinki = from the party).
над (nad = over) takes the instrumental case: над озером (nad ozerom = over the lake).
шли (shli = were going) comes from идти (idti), the one-direction verb for a single trip toward рынок (rynok = market).
часто (chasto = often) triggers the round-trip verb: бегал (begal = ran there and back), not one-way бежал (bezhal).
носить (nosit) means carry, but with очки (ochki = glasses) or clothes it means wear: носит очки (nosit ochki = wears glasses).
помогать (pomogat) takes the dative, so the person helped is мне (mne = me), not accusative: помогал мне (pomogal mne = helped me).
Being late uses опоздать (opozdat) with на (na) plus accusative: опоздал на работу (opozdal na rabotu = late for work).
звонить (zvonit) takes the dative, so the person you call stands in dative and the question word is кому (komu = to whom), as in звонил (zvonil).
не хватает (ne khvataet = lacks) is impersonal: the person is dative ему (emu = to him) and the missing thing is genitive времени (vremeni = time).
в гости (v gosti = for a visit) is a fixed phrase for going to visit someone, used here with привёл (privyol = brought).
After a large number the noun goes genitive plural: шестьсот граммов (shestsot grammov = six hundred grams).
из-за (iz-za = because of) marks a negative cause and takes the genitive: из-за новостей (iz-za novostey = because of the news).
For transport, на (na) plus the prepositional case means by that vehicle: на метро (na metro = by metro).
Помоги (pomogi = help) is the informal command of помочь (pomoch), the ты (ty) form used with friends, family, or children.
Принесите (prinesite = bring) uses the -ите ending, the polite or plural command form you use with strangers.
за собой (za soboy = behind oneself) uses the reflexive pronoun себя (sebya), which points back to the subject of the command.
через (cherez = in) plus accusative gives time from now: через десять минут (cherez desyat minut = in ten minutes).
несёт (nesyot = is carrying) is from нести (nesti), used for carrying something in hand while on foot in one direction.
предложили (predlozhili = offered) is 3rd-person plural with no subject, meaning she was offered: Ей (Yey = to her) is dative.
вёл (vyol = was leading) is from вести (vesti), used for leading a person or animal on foot: вёл коня (vyol konya = led a horse).
радоваться (radovatsya) takes the dative, so the thing you are glad about is погоде (pogode = weather): радуемся погоде (raduemsya pogode).
Russian doubles the negative: никому (nikomu = to no one) still needs не (ne) before говори (govori = tell).
The instrumental marks what you wash with: холодной водой (kholodnoy vodoy = with cold water), no preposition needed.
Demonstratives agree in gender: этот (etot) for masculine nouns like товар (tovar = product), эта (eta) for feminine, это (eto) for neuter.
